name: marisa
desc: Matching Algorithm with Recursively Implemented StorAge
why: A compact recursive trie library with a neat data structure idea, though it is mostly a linkable library.

brief.what_it_is: MARISA (Matching Algorithm with Recursively Implemented StorAge) is a static, space-efficient trie data structure, implemented as the C++ library libmarisa. The package also ships command-line tools for building and querying a MARISA-based dictionary: marisa-build, marisa-lookup, marisa-reverse-lookup, marisa-common-prefix-search, marisa-predictive-search, marisa-dump and marisa-benchmark. A dictionary supports lookup (is this string a key?), reverse lookup (restore a key from its ID), common prefix search (find keys that are prefixes of a given string) and predictive search (find keys starting with a given string). The README does not spell out the exact input and output formats of each tool.
brief.why_it_exists: The README's stated advantage is size: libmarisa's dictionary is considerably more compact than other implementations. Its benchmark uses all English Wikipedia page titles (about 9.8 million keys, 200 MB plain) and reports 50.8 MB for marisa-trie against 376.6 MB for darts-clone and 127.7 MB for tx-trie.
brief.how_it_works: The README gives little mechanism detail beyond the name, which spells out Matching Algorithm with Recursively Implemented StorAge. It calls the structure a static trie, meaning the dictionary is built once from a key set and then queried. The deeper internals are in the linked docs, which I did not fetch.

commands_seen.context: Fetches the source from GitHub; the README says this is how to get the latest version.
Configures a Release build in build-rel with native code enabled and tests turned off.
Compiles libmarisa and the command-line tools.
Installs the library and the binaries system-wide.
Installs only the library, without the binaries.

brief.install_notes: Build from source with CMake; the README does not mention brew. Steps are git clone, cmake configure with Release, -DENABLE_NATIVE_CODE=ON and -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF, cmake --build, then sudo cmake --install. The install can be split into Library and Binaries components. No accounts, runtimes or hardware are mentioned.
brief.standout: Compared with double-array tries and LOUDS tries, it aims for a much smaller footprint while still supporting reverse lookup and both prefix-style searches. Its own size table is the main evidence for that trade-off.
brief.status: Likely maintained, but unconfirmed. The README lists latest version 0.3.1 and the project is hosted under s-yata/marisa-trie. I did not see a release date or last-commit date in the README, so I cannot say how recently it was updated.
brief.caveats: The structure is static, so the README gives no sign of incremental updates after building. The size comparison comes from one 2012 dataset and is self-reported by the author. The README mentions no Homebrew packaging, and the brew caveats field is empty. The license is BSD-2-Clause OR LGPL-2.1-or-later, so you choose one. The scout note calls it mostly a linkable library, and the README agrees the library is the main artifact; the CLI tools are secondary. The README's usage examples are missing, so I could not verify any tool's exact syntax.
quotes: Matching Algorithm with Recursively Implemented StorAge (MARISA) is a static and space-efficient trie data structure.
The biggest advantage of libmarisa is that its dictionary size is considerably more compact than others.
